reason: Survives. Fetched the archive.org OCR of dostoevskyletter00dostuoft (Chatto and Windus, 1923, trans. S. S. Koteliansky and J. Middleton Murry). The letter is headed The Peter and Paul Fortress, December 22, 1849, and addressed to Mihail Mihailovich Dostoevsky; the text runs from p. 5 to p. 12. The quotation (Life is a gift, life is happiness, each minute might have been an age of happiness.) sits verbatim on p. 11 under the running head LETTER TO HIS BROTHER 11, and it ends at the translator’s full stop before Si jeunesse savait! This is the Koteliansky and Murry wording, not the Mayne wording (every minute can be an eternity of happiness), so the named translation matches. The context is regret for wasted time, which turns at once to rebirth and hope: gratitude and mortality both, and nothing graphic in the sentence. A small point: the translation spells the brother Mihail, and the section title puts the letter at page 1 only because an editorial preface opens there. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, Dostoevsky 2 of 3 (months 1 and 2), so this line brings him to 3 of 3; not banned. Correspondence is the right form. The source line leads with the name, has no dash, and runs about 125 characters.
